author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Test name 'processFindFormWithPageBelowOneIsClampedToFirstPage' names the production method and describes implementation mechanics rather than observable behavior. The BDD naming school (testing-principles.md § Test Naming, effective 2026-07-31) requires 'the{Subject}Should{Outcome}'. This test is new (2026-08-22) so the school applies in full. A conforming name: 'theOwnerListShouldShowFirstPageWhenPageBelowOneIsRequested'.

Edge-case coverage is incomplete. The production fix 'Math.max(page, 1)' clamps all integers below 1 (page=0, page=-1, page=-999). The test exercises only page=0. Negative page values are a distinct input class not covered. The checklist (test-review skill § Parameterized Tests) calls for '@ParameterizedTest' with '@CsvSource' when multiple cases share the same behavior. A '@CsvSource' row for page=0 and at least one negative value (e.g., page=-1) is required to make the test a complete specification of the clamp.
No blank line separates the Arrange phase (stub setup, line 153-154) from the Act+Assert phase (line 155). testing-principles.md § Four-Phase Test Structure requires phases separated by blank lines.
findings.fix: Insert a blank line between the 'when(...)' stub and the 'mockMvc.perform(...)' call.

findings.description: Variable 'tasks' holds a 'Page<Owner>' but the name carries no domain meaning and is not prefixed 'SOME_' or 'ANY_'. This is a Tier 3 mystery name. Since this test is new (2026-08-22) the three-tier naming convention (testing-principles.md § Three-Tier Data Naming) applies. Rename to 'somePage' or 'SOME_OWNERS_PAGE' to signal that the exact contents are irrelevant to the outcome under test.

approved_aspects: MockMvc real-HTTP-layer usage is correct — the test drives the framework's real dispatch and binding machinery, satisfying the mocking policy for web-layer tests
The page=0 case does reproduce the bug: without the clamp, PageRequest.of(-1, size) throws and the response is 500, which the status().isOk() assertion catches
AssertJ / MockMvc result-matcher chains are used correctly; no JUnit assertEquals calls present
The mock stub pattern follows the pre-existing suite convention, which testing-principles.md explicitly tolerates for the existing test class

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: Test method name follows implementation naming ('processFindForm...') rather than the BDD school mandated by testing-principles.md § Test Naming for tests added 2026-07-31 onward. The name describes what is called, not what must be true. Rename to something like 'theOwnerListShouldRenderWhenPageIsZero' or 'theOwnerSearchShouldClampNonPositivePageToFirstPage'.
findings.fix: Rename the test method to the{Subject}Should{Outcome} form, e.g. theOwnerListShouldRenderWhenPageIsZero.

findings.description: Variable named 'tasks' holds a Page<Owner>. The name is a domain-unrelated copy-paste from other methods in the file. Per testing-principles.md § Three-Tier Data Naming, irrelevant fixtures use the SOME_/ANY_ naming tier or an anonymous factory; a domain-wrong name that obscures what the variable holds falls into the Tier 3 (mystery) category and must be eliminated. The same mis-naming exists throughout the file (pre-existing debt) but a newly added test must not perpetuate it.
findings.fix: Rename to 'ownersPage' or 'twoOwners' to make the domain and purpose clear.

findings.description: 'new Owner()' constructs a production type directly. Testing-principles.md § Test Data Construction (applies to tests added 2026-07-31 onward) requires construction behind a factory method: 'a slice adding a test writes it behind one from the start.' The second Owner in the list exists only to raise the count above 1 (so the controller takes the list branch); that role should be expressed via an anonymous factory such as anyOwner().
findings.fix: Introduce an anyOwner() factory method (parallel to the existing george() factory) that creates a minimal, unnamed Owner, and replace 'new Owner()' with anyOwner().

findings.description: The test asserts HTTP 200 and view name but does not verify which Pageable the repository received. The implicit proof (a 500 would occur if PageRequest.of(-1, 5) were constructed) is correct but fragile: a future guard that converts the exception to a 400 would make this test pass while the clamp is absent. A verify call confirming PageRequest.of(0, 5) (0-indexed first page) was passed would make the contract explicit and survive that change.
findings.fix: Add: verify(this.owners).findByLastNameStartingWith(anyString(), eq(PageRequest.of(0, 5))); after the mockMvc.perform call.

approved_aspects: Production fix is minimal and placed at the correct point: the clamp fires before findPaginatedForOwnersLastName calls PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize), so page=0 would have produced PageRequest.of(-1, 5) without it
Math.max(page, 1) is idiomatic Java; the reassignment at the top of the method means all downstream uses see the normalized value without scatter
The inline comment adds 'why' context (out-of-range requests return a listing, not an error) that the expression alone does not carry
Test is a direct reproducer: it would fail without the clamp because Spring Data rejects a negative page index
checkJavaFormat task absent from this build is a pre-existing toolchain gap, not introduced by this change
